findings.title: NX069 qualification manufactures or launders decisive PASS fields
findings.observed: PASS and zero fields are preassigned, synthetic, shallowly detector-checked, or accepted from stale/unbound artifacts; dirty source is explicitly ignored by a PASS branch.
findings.expected: Fresh exact-HEAD exact-TREE execution with closed producer lineage and detector mutation coverage.
findings.invariant: Machine-readable qualification verdict derives from raw current observations rather than producer assertions.
findings.failure_sequence: Producer emits literal PASS/zero or stale aggregate; shallow detector sees no direct final-field literal; aggregate ignores source cleanliness or lacks binding; NX069 reports PASS.
findings.counterargument: A newer JUnit file reports zero failures and a 60-second soak artifact exists.
findings.falsification: Those files lack one complete binding to current HEAD/TREE/test manifest; source code still permits synthetic fallback and manufactured decisive fields.
findings.impact: Current release qualification is invalidated; no runtime exploit is inferred.
findings.siblings: Gate producers and anti-hardcode detector searched; same constant/default/caller/stale classes confirmed in security, soak, performance, Windows and UAC producers.
findings.required_action: Replace self-reporting with raw producer evidence and mutation-test the detector.
findings.requalification: Full source-bound qualification required after repair.

findings.title: Canonical task completion trusts submitted repository evidence and criterion assertions
findings.entrypoint: Browser content adapter to m9b_native_host project_execution_submit
findings.observed: Submitter controls status, head_after, evidence references and criterion type; a manual criterion retyped DETERMINISTIC with no evidence completes the task.
findings.expected: Git and evidence are dereferenced by canonical authority and criterion type remains plan-owned.
findings.invariant: Untrusted result transport cannot self-authorize canonical completion.
findings.failure_sequence: Create valid binding; submit matching envelope with PASS, null head_after, empty evidence and manual criterion typed DETERMINISTIC; acceptance becomes PASS and task becomes completed.
findings.counterargument: Binding, command, correlation, plan, task, repo alias and head_before are validated.
findings.falsification: Those checks are real but do not observe head_after/evidence or prevent criterion reclassification; counterexample remains accepted.
findings.impact: Task and AUTO progression can advance without required review or authoritative result facts.
findings.siblings: Same declaration-replaces-observation class confirmed in F-001; identity envelope controls were separately recorded as sound.
findings.required_action: Bind acceptance to plan-owned criterion types and authoritative Git/evidence readers.
findings.requalification: Focused acceptance, replay, stale-result and manual-review adversarial matrix.

findings.title: Project Memory and Catalog locks reclaim a live owner by age
findings.entrypoint: GUI Project Center and vNext Native Host project workflows
findings.observed: A lock older than 120 seconds is unlinked without proving owner death or process incarnation.
findings.expected: A live owner keeps exclusivity regardless of suspension duration.
findings.invariant: No two writers may occupy one project/catalog critical section.
findings.failure_sequence: Writer A acquires; pauses over 120 seconds; B deletes A lock and enters; A resumes; both publish competing state.
findings.counterargument: Normal critical sections are short and include token checks at release.
findings.falsification: Suspend/sleep is protocol-reachable; harness used the current process PID and B still reclaimed immediately; release token does not restore lost exclusivity.
findings.impact: Lost updates and inconsistent canonical project state.
findings.siblings: Five identified exclusive-create token locks searched; age-only live reclaim confirmed in 2/5; stable-handle Bootstrap and single-root locks refute overgeneralization.
findings.required_action: Use stable OS ownership or incarnation-aware lease protocol.
findings.requalification: Multi-process suspend, replacement, crash and retry matrix.

findings.title: Exclusive-create token locks publish invalid metadata and delete replacement owners
findings.entrypoint: Project queue, catalog, memory, environment cache and shared-resource writers
findings.observed: Final lock pathname exists before complete metadata; release/reclaim compare token then unlink pathname; queue refuses malformed lock forever.
findings.expected: Ownership publication is atomic and release cannot remove a different incarnation.
findings.invariant: Only the observed owner object may be reclaimed or released; malformed creation remains recoverable.
findings.failure_sequence: Create final path; fail/short-write metadata causing permanent queue busy, or replace lock after token read and before unlink so prior owner deletes new owner.
findings.counterargument: O_EXCL, tokens, PID checks and foreign-owner nominal tests exist.
findings.falsification: Existing tests are sequential; deterministic replacement injection deleted B in queue/shared/cache, while failed queue metadata left a zero-byte unreclaimable lock.
findings.impact: Concurrent writers, lost ownership, or permanent queue/cache liveness loss.
findings.siblings: 5/5 identified exclusive-create token lock protocols have at least one publication or compare-unlink issue; OS-handle locks are not affected.
findings.required_action: Publish validated metadata atomically and use stable-handle/atomic ownership release.
findings.requalification: Process-level ABA, short-write, kill and malformed-lock matrix across 5/5 protocols.

findings.title: Launch outbox and queue projection do not converge after TTL expiry
findings.observed: Queue expiry removes a PUBLISHED projection; reconciler scans only PENDING outbox rows and leaves the queue empty.
findings.expected: Every non-acknowledged canonical launch converges to one consumable projection or explicit blocked state.
findings.invariant: Canonical launch state and downstream queue eventually converge after restart/expiry.
findings.failure_sequence: Prepare and publish launch; mark outbox PUBLISHED; advance beyond 10-minute TTL; peek clears queue; reconcile sees no PENDING record; outbox remains PUBLISHED and queue remains empty.
findings.counterargument: Normal publish is prepare-before-projection and sequential replay is idempotent.
findings.falsification: Those strengths cover PENDING and same-launch replay, not PUBLISHED-without-projection; executed counterexample produced reconciled_count zero.
findings.impact: Lost continuation/launch with canonical state falsely implying publication.
findings.siblings: Orphan replacement race remains narrower because reconciler has no product caller; PUBLISHED/TTL asymmetry is on the reachable publish model.
findings.required_action: Reconcile every non-acknowledged durable state with fenced projection identity at startup/use.
findings.requalification: Expiry, restart, orphan replacement and ACK-boundary matrix.

findings.title: CURRENT lifecycle documentation is stale and overstates closure
findings.observed: Document says NX071 NOT STARTED and qualification/AUTO are closed although later source and current evidence contradict those claims.
findings.expected: CURRENT projection is regenerated from current authority and qualified evidence.
findings.invariant: Operator-facing current state must not conflate historical qualification, current source and active deployment.
findings.failure_sequence: Operator consumes committed CURRENT doc after later commits and treats stale PASS/not-started statements as current.
findings.counterargument: Document explicitly explains source versus production and may be a point-in-time snapshot.
findings.falsification: It labels the table Current status and is two commits behind; exact source/deployment distinction text is sound but does not cure stale task and qualification claims.
findings.impact: Incorrect release/operator decisions, not direct runtime corruption.
findings.siblings: Other historical docs were not promoted to defects; only explicit CURRENT claims are affected.
findings.required_action: Regenerate current status from authoritative lifecycle/evidence inputs.
findings.requalification: Documentation consistency gate after evidence repair.

findings.title: GUI AUTO Start/Stop and Browser/Native AUTO use split authorities
findings.entrypoint: default Project Center GUI Start Auto and Stop Auto
findings.observed: GUI writes v2 cursor/fence while live Browser/Native execution consumes v1 milestone run/bindings/queue.
findings.expected: User-visible AUTO controls and executing path share one authority and STOP fence.
findings.invariant: Accepted Start produces runnable execution; accepted Stop prevents later effects in that run.
findings.failure_sequence: GUI Start returns AUTO_STARTED but creates no v1 binding/queue; or preexisting v1 run remains RUNNABLE after GUI returns STOPPED in v2.
findings.counterargument: v2 may be intended future authority and v1 remains production during migration.
findings.falsification: The default GUI exposes v2 commands as canonical while current native workflow consumes v1; no bridge was found and dynamic snapshots diverge.
findings.impact: False start acknowledgement and ineffective stop safety boundary.
findings.siblings: Start and Stop both reproduced; later task execution and queue consumption were traced to v1.
findings.required_action: Choose one authority or provide fenced transactional bridge.
findings.requalification: End-to-end GUI to Native/Browser start-stop process tests.

findings.title: Plan activation is not atomic across plan pointer memory and catalog
findings.observed: Plan file/current pointer publish precedes memory event/execution/catalog update with no common journal, recovery or target CAS.
findings.expected: All plan authority projections commit atomically or converge via reachable recovery.
findings.invariant: Current plan bytes, pointer digest, execution prerequisites and catalog version describe one generation.
findings.failure_sequence: Publish v2 pointer; fail before memory transaction; reopen sees v2 plan but no PLAN_UPDATED event; same-byte retry rejected as successor required.
findings.counterargument: Each individual file uses atomic replace and updates are version checked.
findings.falsification: Per-file atomicity does not cover multi-domain transition; injected boundary produced durable split state and non-retriable recovery.
findings.impact: Plan authority divergence, blocked retry and incorrect execution/catalog projections.
findings.siblings: Same multi-domain transition class confirmed in F-005/F-007/F-009; no common transaction found.
findings.required_action: Journal/fence the transition and make replay converge from any durable prefix.
findings.requalification: Crash at every publication boundary plus concurrent same-version writers.

findings.title: Conversation binding commits before launch claim ownership
findings.observed: Conversation is persisted after peek and before queue.claim succeeds.
findings.expected: Conversation ownership linearizes with successful queue claim.
findings.invariant: A losing claimant cannot mutate canonical conversation ownership.
findings.failure_sequence: Peek observes launch; bind conversation commits; competing claim wins before caller CAS; queue.claim returns none; losing conversation remains bound.
findings.counterargument: Binding is one-time and claim usually follows immediately under queue lock.
findings.falsification: Binding and queue use separate critical sections; forced losing CAS returned busy_or_missing while losing conversation persisted.
findings.impact: Rightful claimant can be blocked or results bound to the wrong conversation.
findings.siblings: Order-of-commit review covered publish, ACK and outbox transitions; this exact pre-claim canonical mutation was confirmed.
findings.required_action: Claim first and bind under one fenced ownership transition or compensate safely.
findings.requalification: Concurrent claims, crash between claim/bind and retry matrix.

findings.title: Output limit applies after unbounded process-output accumulation
findings.observed: Runner collects and joins full output before producing a 64 KiB inline bound.
findings.expected: Capture enforces byte bound while reading or spills with bounded memory.
findings.invariant: Declared output bound limits parent resource acquisition.
findings.failure_sequence: Allowed child writes 8 MiB; parent accumulates 8 MiB and peaks near 17.1 MiB; only final inline content truncates to 65,536 characters.
findings.counterargument: Timeout bounds duration and current product call graph does not reach the runner.
findings.falsification: Timeout does not bound output rate; finding severity is narrowed to latent because product reachability was not established.
findings.impact: Memory exhaustion if wired to untrusted/high-output processes.
findings.siblings: Local worker simulated backend and runner callers searched; no deployed product caller found.
findings.required_action: Stream with hard cap/spill/terminate before accumulation if wired.
findings.requalification: High-rate stdout/stderr process tests and resource ceilings.

findings.title: ProjectScopeCoordinator ignores failed cursor CAS
findings.observed: CAS false is discarded and caller receives a run identity absent from durable cursor.
findings.expected: Failed CAS fails closed or returns the committed competing identity.
findings.invariant: Returned authority corresponds to durable committed state.
findings.failure_sequence: Force update_cursor_cas false; helper returns new run ID; durable row retains a different run ID.
findings.counterargument: No current production caller was found and outer transaction may serialize typical use.
findings.falsification: Counterexample proves symbol defect but reachability search narrows runtime impact to latent.
findings.impact: Stale/non-authoritative run identity if later wired.
findings.siblings: CAS-return consumers searched; no same product-reachable discard established.
findings.required_action: Check CAS result and propagate only committed identity.

findings.title: Project single-flight is enforced per execution ID rather than per project
findings.observed: Submission excludes PENDING rows and claim CAS scopes only execution_id; two mutating rows for one project both become CLAIMED.
findings.expected: At most one project-mutating local effect can be pending/claimed/running for a project.
findings.invariant: PROJECT_SIMULTANEOUS_LOCAL_EFFECTS_MAX equals one across distinct execution IDs.
findings.failure_sequence: Submit mutation A and B for same project while both PENDING; both pass count; claim A by ID; claim B by different ID; both claims succeed.
findings.counterargument: SQLite serializes each transaction and the existing contention test proves one owner.
findings.falsification: Serialization does not help because sequential submissions are both legal; test contends on one execution ID and proves only per-ID ownership.
findings.impact: Concurrent project mutations and state corruption if worker is wired to real effects.
findings.siblings: Project-wide declarations compared with DB constraints and claim predicates; this is the confirmed mismatch; product callers were not found.
findings.required_action: Enforce project-wide active mutation uniqueness transactionally including PENDING.
findings.requalification: Distinct-ID multi-process project contention and lease-expiry matrix.
